summary: Architecture authority for Hoplight's product shape: package layout under a future vaudeville-studios monorepo, the hub-and-spoke canonical model with escrow, agent design lessons from RoleCall Orison, productions as project workspaces, dual faces (CLI and Studio), and security and privacy invariants. The planned packages tree keeps core free of other package deps, with formats, lore, presets, macros, regexkit, assembly, ai, agent, doctor, and interview as pure engine packages, and cli plus studio apps that import packages only. Dependency rule is core left-arrow formats left-arrow everything; ai and agent never import UI; apps never import each other or get imported by packages. Canonical codecs always emit data plus EscrowEnvelope so origin-format fields round-trip; codecs declare capabilities for honest convert reports. Agent design requires a tiny always-on tool surface, resource-model verbs over vaud URIs, spill store for large tool results, staged edits only, model capability profiles, and an early eval harness. Productions are folders with readable files, vaud.json, and content-addressed history. Faces are scriptable CLI plus agent REPL, and a later Studio face over the same engine with no private engine capabilities. Network is limited to configured model providers and checksum-verified GitHub Releases updates; keys use OS keychain or encrypted file; no telemetry.

sections.title: Product repo layout (the future `vaudeville-studios` code repo)
sections.summary: Describes the planned vaudeville-studios monorepo layout. packages/core owns zod schemas for character, lorebook, preset, persona, regex-script, and world or compendium, plus escrow envelope, IDs, and token counting interfaces, with zero deps on other packages. packages/formats holds one codec module per external format implementing detect, parse, serialize, and capabilities, including PNG tEXt chunk IO. lore, presets, macros, and regexkit extract engine pieces from prior VAUDEVILLE work. assembly builds Test Stage prompt payloads with a full trace. ai covers provider adapters, streaming, tool-calling with weak-model fallback, and key vault. agent owns the turn loop, deferred tool schemas, spill store, compaction, staged-edit envelope, and persona loader. doctor and interview own audit and Table Read engines as UI-agnostic packages. apps/cli is vaud compiled with bun build --compile; apps/studio is the M6 Tauri face. fixtures hold the Round-Trip Law corpus. Dependency rule: core then formats then everything; ai and agent never import UI; apps import packages only and never each other; no package imports from apps.

sections.title: The canonical model + escrow (ADR-005, spec: specs/formats/canonical-model.md)
sections.summary: Internal model is a superset of every supported format. Every codec parse must produce CanonicalX data plus EscrowEnvelope holding source format, version, and unmapped origin fields. Serializing back merges escrow in; that is the Round-Trip Law. Codecs declare capabilities so vaud convert can report escrowed fields honestly. Authority: ADR-005 and specs/formats/canonical-model.md.

sections.title: The agent (lessons imported from RoleCall's Orison work)
sections.summary: Agent design constraints imported from RoleCall Orison. Keep a tiny always-on tool surface of meta-tools and defer everything else, revealing schemas on demand, because accuracy collapses past roughly fifty loaded tools. Prefer a resource model of ls, read, write, and search over a vaud URI space covering production files, fixtures, and settings instead of many noun-specific tools so weak models can drive four verbs. Spill store sends tool results above about one thousand tokens to disk with a handle and peek so the agent greps and reads handles while context stays small. Staged edits only: the agent never mutates a user file directly; it stages a diff envelope, validation runs, the user approves with optional auto-approve, then commit, and every commit is a version in production history. Model capability profiles use native tool-calling when available, prompted XML fallback otherwise, explicit samplers, and one tool call per turn on weak models. Eval harness arrives early in M2 with golden tasks against a model matrix; agent changes must move tokens-per-task or success-rate, not vibes.

sections.title: Productions (project workspaces)
sections.summary: A production is a folder of human-readable JSON and Markdown files, a vaud.json manifest, and a .vaud/history/ tree of content-addressed snapshots. History has no git dependency but remains git-friendly. Library mode is a managed default production for loose-file users. vaud commands also accept bare file paths so users are not forced into a full workspace to run single-file operations.

sections.title: Faces
sections.summary: Two product faces share one engine. The CLI exposes plain scriptable commands with JSON output flags, and bare vaud opens the agent REPL. Studio is planned for M6 as Tauri plus a local UI over the same engine through a thin IPC layer. Every studio action must map to an engine call the CLI can also express. The studio is forbidden from having private engine capabilities that the CLI cannot reach.

sections.title: Security & privacy invariants
sections.summary: Binding security and privacy rules. No network calls except model providers the user configured and the updater hitting GitHub Releases with checksum verification; both paths are auditable in source. Keys live in the OS keychain where available, otherwise an AES-encrypted file with a local secret. No telemetry of any kind. Crash reports are local files the user can choose to share; nothing is uploaded automatically.
